title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to quantify the marginal detection benefit of automated sandboxed emulation over a strong deterministic validator for LLM-generated network-configuration artifacts. Under a preregistered paired-binary design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) we produced Npairs = 720 intent→configuration tasks using the declared model (gpt-5-mini) with shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation shared across paired conditions). Conditions: (A) baseline = deterministic validator-only (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); (B) guarded = same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation. Results (complete paired set): baseline detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded detected 720/720 = 1.0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest used for power planning was 0.20 (20 percentage points); the observed effect is far below that threshold. We report the preregistered design, exact archived sampling settings, and limitations that bound external generalization.

sections.introduction:
Generative models that translate operator intent into executable network configuration are increasingly proposed as components of NetOps/AIOps workflows. Operational safety for such agentic pipelines typically depends on surrounding tooling—deterministic validators, formal verifiers, and sandboxed execution—rather than the model alone [1], [2]. Prior work advocates generate→validate→repair pipelines and prototype sandboxed validation, but quantitative cross-vendor evaluations of how much runtime emulation adds beyond a strong static validator remain limited [2], [3].

Research question. For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired-binary experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) executed end-to-end. (2) Artifact-grounded quantitative results on Npairs = 720 showing a vanishing aggregate guarded benefit in this setting. (3) A focused analysis of explanatory factors, threats to validity, and operational implications supporting careful interpretation and follow-up studies.
sections.related_work: Surveys and system papers document growing use of LLMs for intent-driven configuration and emphasize workflow-centred mitigations—deterministic validators, verifiers, and sandboxed emulation—to reduce operational risk [1], [2]. Tool and prototype work demonstrates generate→validate→repair patterns and shows that emulation or formal analysis can reveal runtime failures missed by static checks [2], [3]. Empirical studies in closely related domains (code/specification generation) report that LLMs often produce incorrect outputs and that external verifiers substantially reduce error prevalence, but they also highlight wide variability across tasks, validators, and models and call for narrow, workflow-centred evaluations to map where guarded stages add value [2], [3]. Our experiment operationalizes a narrowly scoped instance of these recommendations by measuring the marginal guarded-stage detection gain against a strong deterministic validator on a synthetic task bank.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) was frozen before execution. Design: paired-binary with shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation shared across the paired conditions), Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks and planned episodes = 1440. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest used in power planning was 0.20 (20 percentage points) with target ≈80% power under conservative baseline-rate assumptions; this design sensitivity is reported because the observed effect was much smaller.

Task bank and inclusion. Confirmatory tasks were synthetic intent→configuration items (intent_configuration_repair_v1 family) covering abstracted vendor-CLI families and a small set of topology templates. Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance per the preregistration; deterministic parser reseed and replacement policies were applied as specified. The run recorded no irrecoverable parser exclusions for the confirmatory set.

Model, prompts, and sampling. Declared/requested model: gpt-5-mini (provider entry: openai_responses). Execution settings archived: max_output_tokens = 2000; temperature unset (null) — therefore client-side sampling determinism was not imposed. Execution accounting: maximum_model_calls planned = 1440; model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial generations plus one repair-stage call).

Validator and guarded pipeline. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline condition = deterministic validator-only. Guarded condition = deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation that observes runtime behavior beyond static rule checks. Per the preregistration, generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: the identical initial LLM output was used for both baseline and guarded conditions for every pair. This design implies that any between-condition discordance can arise only from (a) guarded-stage emulation observations or (b) the single recorded post-generation repair call; it does not reflect differences in initial model outputs.

Analysis. Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. We report exact McNemar two-sided test results plus a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and replacement followed the preregistered deterministic policies; no preregistration deviations affected the confirmatory analysis.
sections.results:
Confirmatory outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720). Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667].

Missingness and preregistration compliance. The analysis used complete_pair_count = 720; there were no exclusions and no preregistration deviations recorded that affect the confirmatory estimand. All prompts, responses, validator traces, emulation outputs, and analysis artifacts were archived per the preregistration.

Interpretation. The preregistered minimum detectable effect for which the study was powered was 0.20 (20 percentage points). The observed point estimate (~0.0014) lies well below that design target and therefore the study was not sensitive to large but rare guarded benefits under this synthetic, high-coverage setting. The numerical results reported above are artifact-grounded and identical to the archived analysis outputs.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded benefit negligible in this run? The archived artifacts support three primary explanatory factors: (1) ceiling effect — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 achieved near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic misconfigurations present in the synthetic task bank, leaving little room for emulation to add detections; (2) task curation — parser-validated, synthetic tasks reduce noisy or adversarial inputs and therefore increase validator effectiveness relative to production-like distributions; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics — identical initial generations across conditions constrain discordance sources to guarded-stage observations or the limited repair activity (the execution manifest records a single repair call).

Operational implications. When a high-coverage static validator exists and input artifacts closely match validator rule coverage, adding sandboxed emulation can yield negligible marginal detection gains at the aggregate level. This does not imply emulation is unnecessary: heterogeneous vendor behaviors, weaker validators, adversarial misconfigurations, stateful runtime interactions, or production-scale topologies can create regimes where emulation provides substantive additional detections.

Recommendations. To map operational regimes where guarded stages materially improve safety, future work should (a) evaluate broader and adversarial task banks, (b) compare multiple model and validator families, and (c) employ higher-fidelity emulation that better approximates vendor/OS nuances and scale effects. These are proposals for follow-up experiments; they are not new claims about the present data.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator against the same validator augmented with automated sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Aggregated over 720 paired tasks, the guarded pipeline yielded a negligible absolute detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. The result reflects a likely ceiling effect of the task bank and validator used and must be interpreted with the preregistered power target (minimum detectable effect = 0.20) in mind. Artifact-grounded analysis is archived and we recommend targeted follow-up studies that expand task diversity and adversarial scope to identify regimes where sandboxed execution adds substantive value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier or adversarial inputs.
Single model family (declared/requested: gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.
Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation shared across paired conditions) constrain discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.
Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to production vendor/OS behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; scale and vendor nuances may change outcomes.

The study was powered for a preregistered minimum detectable effect of 0.20 (20 percentage points). The observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity; absence of a large aggregated guarded benefit in this experiment does not imply the guarded pipeline is never valuable in other operational regimes.
